paragraphs: An observed association between two variables does not, by itself, explain how one influences the other. Causal mediation analysis studies how causal effects pass through different mechanisms, but spurious associations also need explanation. This paper asks how variation that is not a causal effect can be separated into contributions connected to the underlying causal structure.

The authors develop formal decomposition tools for both Markovian and Semi-Markovian causal models. Their results allow spurious effects to be decomposed nonparametrically, without restricting the analysis to a particular parametric form. They also provide sufficient conditions for identifying these decompositions: conditions under which the components can be recovered from the available information.

The contribution is an explanatory framework for associations that conventional causal-effect decomposition does not directly address. It connects the question of whether an association is causal to the further question of which mechanisms produce its spurious part. The authors demonstrate applications empirically and identify uses in explainable and fair AI, epidemiology, and medicine. Recovery remains tied to the stated sufficient identification conditions.
neurips-2023-a-causal-framework-for-deco.tldr: The paper develops nonparametric tools and sufficient identification conditions for decomposing spurious associations into contributions from underlying causal mechanisms.

paragraphs: Graph networks usually treat node relabeling consistently: changing node names changes the output labels accordingly. This paper distinguishes that property from transformations of a signal on a fixed domain. When the graph stays fixed, the relevant exact symmetries are its automorphisms, transformations that preserve the graph itself. Real graphs often have few such symmetries.

The authors therefore study approximate symmetries, formalized through graph coarsening. This creates a way to impose useful shared structure even when the original graph lacks exact symmetry. A bias-variance formula describes the resulting tradeoff: stronger symmetry constraints can make an estimator more regular, while also reducing the range of functions it can express.

Experiments examine different symmetry choices in image inpainting, traffic prediction, and human pose estimation. Together with the theory, they show that the best generalization can come from a suitably chosen group larger than the exact automorphism group but smaller than all node permutations. The result makes the amount of imposed symmetry a meaningful modeling choice.
neurips-2023-approximately-equivariant-g.tldr: Approximate graph symmetries offer a tunable tradeoff between expressivity and regularity that can improve generalization beyond exact graph symmetries.

paragraphs: A classifier becomes vulnerable when a small input change can cross its decision boundary. Methods intended to improve robustness do not necessarily enlarge the distance between examples and that boundary. This paper targets that distance directly through a differentiable regularizer that provides a lower bound on the input-space margin.

Computing the regularizer requires information about how rapidly the network can change along certain directions, expressed through Lipschitz constants. The authors develop a scalable procedure for obtaining guaranteed, differentiable upper bounds on those constants. Relatively accurate bounds help avoid excessive regularization and make it possible to influence the decision boundary more directly during training.

The bounding procedure uses the monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity of activation layers. Its bounds also support designing layers whose Lipschitz constants can be controlled. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Tiny-ImageNet report competitive improvements relative to state-of-the-art methods. The contribution connects a geometric robustness objective with a practical way to calculate the bounds that objective needs.
neurips-2023-certified-robustness-via-dy.tldr: A differentiable margin regularizer and improved Lipschitz bounds provide a practical approach to strengthening certified classifier robustness.

paragraphs: A scene representation must adapt when the physical scene changes, while preserving what it already knows about areas that remain the same. Existing approaches for updating neural radiance fields can require substantial new image capture and retraining. CL-NeRF studies continual updates using only a few new images, making adaptation and memory preservation joint objectives.

The method combines two components with distinct roles. A lightweight expert adaptor handles new changes and the evolving scene representation. A conflict-aware knowledge distillation objective helps retain information about unchanged regions. Together, these components address the tension between incorporating new observations and forgetting previously learned parts of the scene.

The authors also introduce a benchmark and evaluation metrics for continual learning of neural radiance fields. Their experiments report high-quality views from new viewpoints in both changed and unchanged regions, alongside efficient training. Compared with existing methods, CL-NeRF improves adaptation and reduces forgetting. The findings support treating scene updates as an ongoing learning problem with explicit mechanisms for both change and retention.
neurips-2023-cl-nerf-continual-learning-.tldr: CL-NeRF updates evolving scenes from a few new images while using an adaptor and knowledge distillation to reduce forgetting.

paragraphs: Cookie consent changes the information available to a recommender, but the consequences may depend on how consent choices differ across demographic groups. This paper investigates that relationship in simulations of a recommender driven by user engagement. It asks how accurately the system can estimate hidden user characteristics, including demographics and tastes.

When consent rates depend on demographics, the simulations show unequal effects on estimation accuracy. Counterintuitively, refusing cookie sharing can sometimes let the recommender estimate a user's attributes more accurately than accepting would. The finding is conditional on the demographic dependence of consent rates; it does not establish that refusal generally reveals more information.

The gap between groups' consent rates amplifies these differences. Among users who consent, those in the lower-consent group generally face larger estimation errors than comparable users in the higher-consent group; the direction reverses among those who refuse. These results motivate fairness criteria that consider whether privacy choices correspond consistently to what a system can infer about people.
neurips-2023-cookie-consent-has-disparat.tldr: Simulations show that demographic differences in cookie consent rates can produce unequal inference accuracy and sometimes make refusal more revealing than consent.

paragraphs: Line search adjusts an optimizer's step size by checking candidate updates. Requiring every accepted step to decrease the current batch objective can make those steps unnecessarily small. This paper studies relaxing that requirement in over-parameterized models, allowing nonmonotone progress so that larger updates may be accepted.

The authors prove convergence rates matching the fast rates of monotone methods despite removing the requirement of consistent objective decrease. They introduce PoNoS, which combines a nonmonotone line search with a Polyak initial step size. A resetting technique further reduces the need to repeatedly shrink candidate steps, eliminating backtracking in most iterations while preserving a large initial step size.

Experiments report faster convergence and improved generalization for SGD and Adam compared with earlier monotone line searches. A runtime comparison also shows that improvements measured across training epochs carry over to overall computation time. This matters because accepting better steps is useful in practice only when the work required to select them does not erase the training gains.
neurips-2023-don-t-be-so-monotone-relaxi.tldr: Nonmonotone stochastic line search permits larger steps, preserves fast convergence guarantees, and improves training speed in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Spectral clustering groups graph vertices by first representing them in a numerical space derived from the graph Laplacian. The standard approach uses k eigenvectors when seeking k clusters. Computing those vectors is expensive enough to dominate the algorithm's runtime, making the embedding stage a natural target for improvement.

This paper replaces that embedding with one using only O(log(k)) vectors computed through the power method. The embedding can be constructed in nearly linear time relative to graph size. The authors also prove recovery of the underlying clusters under assumptions on the input graph, linking the computational shortcut to a conditional correctness guarantee.

Evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets find that the algorithm runs significantly faster than alternative clustering methods while maintaining approximately the same clustering accuracy. The main implication is that the conventional embedding can be substantially simplified without losing comparable empirical quality in the tested settings. The theoretical recovery claim still depends on the graph satisfying the paper's assumptions.
neurips-2023-fast-and-simple-spectral-cl.tldr: A spectral clustering method uses O(log(k)) power-method vectors for faster embeddings, with conditional recovery guarantees and comparable empirical accuracy.

paragraphs: Mean-field neural networks can learn features, and mean-field Langevin dynamics is a noisy gradient procedure with global optimization guarantees. Yet successful optimization alone does not explain whether learned features improve predictions on unseen data or reduce the amount of training data needed. This paper addresses that statistical question for a class of binary classification problems.

The analysis treats training as optimization over a distribution of parameters rather than over one parameter vector. This perspective avoids the usual norm-control approach used in neural-network margin bounds. It yields improved analyses of both sample complexity and convergence, connecting the algorithm's learning behavior to its computational requirements.

The authors apply the framework to k-sparse parity functions. For two-layer networks trained with mean-field Langevin dynamics, they prove a sample-complexity result in which k is decoupled from the exponent governing dependence on input dimension, unlike kernel methods. This provides a concrete theoretical setting where feature learning changes the dimension dependence of the data requirement.
neurips-2023-feature-learning-via-mean-f.tldr: The paper proves statistical benefits of mean-field Langevin feature learning, including improved dimension dependence when learning sparse parity functions.

paragraphs: Combining vehicle sensors with infrastructure sensors can improve perception, but information may arrive at different times and communication capacity is limited. Misaligned observations can weaken the benefit of cooperation. Feature Flow Net addresses both problems in cooperative 3D object detection by modeling how infrastructure features change over time.

Its prediction module uses feature flow to estimate future features and compensate for temporal mismatch. The system transmits this flow instead of feature maps extracted from individual still images, drawing on continuity across successive infrastructure frames. A self-supervised training approach learns feature flow with predictive ability directly from raw infrastructure sequences.

On DAIR-V2X, the reported experiments outperform existing cooperative detection methods while using about one hundredth of the transmission cost of raw data. One model handles all latency conditions covered by the reported evaluation. The result connects communication efficiency with temporal prediction: information about feature evolution can help synchronize shared perception while limiting the amount of data that must be transmitted.
neurips-2023-flow-based-feature-fusion-f.tldr: FFNet shares predictive feature flow to compensate for sensor asynchrony and improve cooperative 3D detection with reduced transmission cost.

paragraphs: Digital agents often interact with graphical interfaces through text representations extracted from HTML or other structured sources. Those representations are not always available, and previous systems have often paired them with actions designed for particular tasks. This paper studies an interface based on screenshots and ordinary keyboard and mouse actions.

The agent receives the visual display as pixels and follows instructions through a generic action space. Building on progress in pixel-based pretraining, the work investigates whether this combination can support effective GUI interaction. The choice matters because both what the agent observes and how it acts correspond to the conceptual interface people commonly use.

The authors show that agents with this setup can outperform human crowdworkers on MiniWob++, a benchmark of GUI instruction-following tasks. The result establishes strong performance for screenshot-based interaction on that benchmark. It demonstrates that access to structured interface text and specially tailored actions is not required for surpassing the reported human comparison in this setting.
neurips-2023-from-pixels-to-ui-actions-l.tldr: Agents using screenshots and generic keyboard and mouse actions can outperform human crowdworkers on the MiniWob++ instruction-following benchmark.

paragraphs: Generating molecules for a protein pocket requires producing realistic three-dimensional structures. Approaches that generate individual atom types and positions can struggle with complicated molecular fragments. D3FG changes the basic representation by treating functional groups as rigid bodies and linkers as point-like components, allowing these pieces to form more complex fragments.

The diffusion model adds noise to component positions, orientations, and types. During generation, denoisers built from equivariant graph neural networks gradually remove that noise from all three variables. This representation lets the model work with the placement and orientation of structured groups while also generating the components that connect them.

Experiments report more realistic 3D molecular structures, competitive affinity toward protein targets, and improved drug properties. The authors also introduce a molecule-elaboration task in which generation builds on existing ligands and protein hotspots. D3FG can generate high-affinity molecules in that setting, extending its use from creating pocket-specific candidates to elaborating candidates from existing molecular and target information.
neurips-2023-functional-group-based-diff.tldr: D3FG generates and elaborates pocket-specific molecules by diffusing functional-group positions, orientations, and types rather than treating every atom independently.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks combine information through aggregation operations such as mean, sum, or maximum. Combining many inputs into one representation inevitably discards information, and different aggregation choices retain different aspects of those inputs. The best choice depends on the problem, yet aggregation often receives less design attention than the network's update modules.

The paper introduces GenAgg, an aggregation operator with a parameterized function space that includes all standard aggregators. This expands the available aggregation choices within a single operator. Its purpose is to make aggregation more adaptable to the task rather than depending only on an initially selected standard function.

Experiments show that GenAgg represents standard aggregators much more accurately than the compared baseline methods. Replacing an existing GNN aggregator with GenAgg also often produces substantial performance improvements across tasks. These findings suggest that aggregation itself is a useful source of model flexibility. The reported gains are frequent rather than universal, consistent with the paper's emphasis on problem-dependent information loss.
neurips-2023-generalised-f-mean-aggregat.tldr: GenAgg parameterizes a family containing standard graph aggregators and often improves GNN performance when substituted for an existing aggregation function.

paragraphs: Language-model generation stores temporary attention information in a key-value cache, whose memory use grows with sequence length and batch size. H2O reduces that cache by exploiting an observed imbalance: a small fraction of tokens contributes most of the value in attention-score computation. The authors call these tokens heavy hitters.

Their investigation finds that heavy hitters correlate strongly with frequent token co-occurrence and that removing them substantially degrades performance. H2O therefore dynamically retains a balance of recent tokens and heavy hitters. The authors formulate eviction as a dynamic submodular problem and provide a theoretical guarantee under mild assumptions.

Accuracy is evaluated with OPT, LLaMA, and GPT-NeoX across multiple tasks. On OPT-6.7B and OPT-30B, the implementation with 20% heavy hitters achieves throughput improvements of up to 29 times over both DeepSpeed Zero-Inference and Hugging Face Accelerate, and up to three times over FlexGen. At the same batch size, latency improves by up to a factor of 1.9. These are reported maximum gains for the evaluated settings.
neurips-2023-h2o-heavy-hitter-oracle-for.tldr: H2O reduces language-model cache memory by retaining recent and attention-heavy tokens, yielding substantial inference speedups in evaluated settings.

paragraphs: Semantic keypoint matching finds corresponding points across images. Representing those points and their relationships as graphs makes graph matching a useful way to solve the problem. This paper argues that existing deep graph matching approaches do not sufficiently capture relative spatial relationships through the way they construct graphs from keypoint coordinates.

The proposed positional reconstruction encoder-decoder, PR-EnDec, learns spatial structure explicitly. Its encoder produces node spatial embeddings with affine transformation invariance. Its decoder reconstructs the graph's locational structure from information contained in node coordinates, encouraging use of higher-order spatial relationships. These two components connect spatial representation learning with a reconstruction objective.

The authors incorporate PR-EnDec into PREGM, an end-to-end graph matching network. Experiments on three public keypoint matching datasets demonstrate the approach's effectiveness. The contribution highlights spatial organization as information that deserves explicit modeling: keypoint correspondence can benefit from representations trained to capture how points are arranged together, beyond what the existing graph construction approaches capture.
neurips-2023-improving-graph-matching-wi.tldr: PREGM improves semantic keypoint matching through an encoder-decoder that learns invariant spatial embeddings and reconstructs graph layout.

paragraphs: Quantization can sharply reduce model performance, and earlier work associated such drops with models exceeding six billion parameters. This paper asks whether size alone explains those cliffs. The question matters because treating the effect as an unavoidable consequence of scale would imply a different route forward than treating it as a consequence of training choices.

The authors investigate training recipes that suppress unusually large activation values. They find that outlier dimensions are sensitive to optimization conditions during pretraining rather than being inherent products of model scale. This supports the possibility of training models in ways that make subsequent quantization less damaging.

The study successfully quantizes models ranging from 410 million to 52 billion parameters with minimal performance degradation. That result provides a counterexample to the idea that quantization cliffs necessarily emerge as models grow. More broadly, the authors raise the possibility that some other apparently emergent behaviors could also depend on optimization or architecture choices, without claiming to establish that for those other behaviors.
neurips-2023-intriguing-properties-of-qu.tldr: Quantization-related activation outliers depend on pretraining conditions, enabling models up to 52 billion parameters to be quantized with minimal degradation.

paragraphs: Continual learning must absorb new tasks without erasing knowledge from earlier ones. It also needs useful confidence estimates when making predictions. NPCL addresses these issues using neural processes, meta-learning models that represent tasks through probability distributions over functions, giving the model a way to express uncertainty alongside its predictions.

The method arranges task-specific modules in a hierarchical latent-variable model. Regularizers act on the learned latent distributions to reduce forgetting as learning proceeds. The same uncertainty estimates can help infer which task head or module to use, connecting confidence assessment to a practical decision inside a continual-learning system.

Experiments report stronger performance than previous continual-learning approaches. The authors also validate uncertainty estimation for identifying novel data and assessing confidence on individual examples. These results support combining knowledge retention with probabilistic task representations. The method's uncertainty output serves both to evaluate predictions and to help select the appropriate module, making uncertainty part of how the system operates.
neurips-2023-npcl-neural-processes-for-u.tldr: NPCL uses hierarchical neural processes to reduce forgetting, estimate predictive uncertainty, and help select task-specific modules during continual learning.

paragraphs: A model of a moving 3D scene can aim beyond reproducing viewpoints during the time covered by training videos. NVFi seeks to learn geometry, appearance, and physical velocity together from multi-view video frames. This broader representation is intended to support prediction of future frames, unsupervised semantic scene decomposition, and motion transfer.

The framework combines a dynamic radiance field at keyframes with a velocity field between frames. A joint optimization module trains the two networks together, connecting the scene's visual representation to its motion across time. This division gives the system explicit components for what the scene looks like and how its contents move.

The authors introduce Dynamic Object and Dynamic Indoor Scene datasets and evaluate the approach across multiple datasets. They report better performance than all compared baselines, particularly for future-frame extrapolation and unsupervised 3D semantic decomposition. The findings support learning velocity alongside geometry and appearance as a useful way to extend dynamic scene modeling beyond view synthesis within the observed period.
neurips-2023-nvfi-neural-velocity-fields.tldr: NVFi jointly learns scene appearance, geometry, and velocity from multi-view videos to support future prediction, scene decomposition, and motion transfer.

paragraphs: Order fulfillment links many sequential decisions, from handling and packing orders to storage, consolidation, pickup, and final delivery. A decision that works well for one unit may interact poorly with decisions elsewhere. This paper studies the full process jointly using multi-agent reinforcement learning rather than optimizing each stage in isolation.

The integrated problem is formulated as a Markov game, with a team of agents learning a joint policy through simulation. The authors create OFCOURSE, a scalable environment in the OpenAI Gym style, to support the complete fulfillment process. Its design allows reproduction, reuse, and customization for different applications.

Within OFCOURSE, the learned policy coordinates order-wise operations across fulfillment units with the objective of minimizing total cost while meeting promised completion times. The authors demonstrate that this joint policy outperforms a combination of locally optimal policies. The result illustrates why coordination across interconnected operations can matter: strong choices for individual stages do not necessarily yield the strongest integrated fulfillment policy.
neurips-2023-ofcourse-a-multi-agent-rein.tldr: OFCOURSE enables joint multi-agent learning across order fulfillment stages, with a learned policy outperforming combined locally optimal policies.

paragraphs: Symbolic models give reinforcement-learning agents a higher-level description of their environment. Such descriptions can guide behavior, but many approaches assume an appropriate symbolic approximation is already available. This paper addresses that dependency by introducing a method that learns optimistic symbolic approximations of the underlying world model.

The learned representations are combined with fast planners that produce diverse plans. Together, these components provide an approach to optimistic exploration in settings where rewards are sparse. The symbolic approximation supplies higher-level guidance, while automated planning turns that representation into possibilities for exploration. Learning the approximation makes its construction part of the method itself.

The authors also investigate whether sharing learned dynamics across similar actions can accelerate learning with minimal human input. They evaluate the method on multiple benchmark domains and compare it with other reinforcement-learning strategies. The stated contribution is a framework joining learned symbolic models, planning, and exploration; the abstract describes the evaluation but does not claim a specific performance advantage from those comparisons.
neurips-2023-optimistic-exploration-in-r.tldr: The method learns optimistic symbolic world models and combines them with diverse planning to guide exploration under sparse rewards.

paragraphs: Few-shot classification uses prior learning to solve new classification tasks from limited examples. Bayesian approaches also characterize uncertainty, but the likelihood used to connect a model to class labels affects its confidence behavior. This paper revisits logistic-softmax, whose conditional conjugacy makes it useful in multiclass Gaussian process classification.

The authors redesign the likelihood with a temperature parameter that controls confidence before observing task data. They show theoretically and empirically that softmax is a special case of logistic-softmax, with logistic-softmax supporting a broader family of data distributions. This clarifies the relationship between the alternatives and provides a mechanism for adjusting prior confidence.

The modified likelihood is incorporated into a deep-kernel Gaussian process meta-learning framework using data augmentation. The authors derive an analytical mean-field approximation for task-specific updates. Their approach produces well-calibrated uncertainty estimates and comparable or better results on standard benchmarks. The contribution combines a more flexible likelihood with an analytical adaptation procedure, addressing predictive performance and uncertainty together.
neurips-2023-revisiting-logistic-softmax.tldr: A temperature-controlled logistic-softmax likelihood broadens Bayesian few-shot classification while supporting calibrated uncertainty and analytical task updates.

paragraphs: Robust estimation seeks a distribution's center even when some samples are corrupted. Heavy-tailed distributions make this difficult, especially when moments such as the mean do not exist. This paper shows that broad classes of symmetric distributions still permit efficient location estimation, including products of symmetric distributions and elliptical distributions.

For the covered product distributions and elliptical distributions with known scatter, the authors obtain error O(ε sqrt(log(1/ε))) under an ε fraction of corruption. This matches the best-known Gaussian error guarantee, with sample requirements matching the cited lower bounds up to a logarithmic dimension factor. Symmetry therefore permits strong guarantees without moment assumptions in these settings.

For elliptical distributions with unknown scatter, a family of algorithms trades greater computational and sample cost for error approaching that rate. The methods combine filtering with Huber-loss techniques to work with better-behaved noise projections. Sum-of-squares proofs supply guarantees even without a first moment. The central distinction is that a symmetric distribution can have an estimable location even when its mean is undefined.
neurips-2023-robust-mean-estimation-with.tldr: Symmetry enables efficient robust location estimation with Gaussian-level error guarantees for broad distribution classes, even without finite moments.

paragraphs: Self-supervised graph learning often borrows propagation-based networks designed for settings with some labels. The paper identifies problems with that choice: shared global parameters can miss local properties, and propagation can mix nodes from different classes. Without labels, this is especially difficult when connected nodes are not predominantly similar.

The authors motivate a different approach through a conditional observation: if propagation within a node's local neighborhood occurred only among same-class nodes, the representation matrix should exhibit low rank. LRD-GNN-Matrix uses low-rank decomposition of the attribute matrix to pursue this structure, offering an alternative to the usual propagation design.

LRD-GNN-Tensor extends the idea to longer-distance information. It constructs an attribute tensor from selected similar local neighborhoods and applies low-rank tensor decomposition. A tensor nuclear norm helps capture relationships between the original neighborhood and those selected neighborhoods. Experiments report superior performance and robustness for the proposed networks, supporting low-rank structure as a useful basis for self-supervised graph representations.
neurips-2023-self-supervised-graph-neura.tldr: LRD-GNNs use low-rank matrix and tensor decompositions to capture local and distant graph structure without conventional propagation-based learning.

paragraphs: Multi-source domain adaptation transfers knowledge from several labeled domains to a target domain without labels. Existing identification approaches can require many domains, restricted transformations of hidden variables, or unchanged label distributions. This paper seeks a less restrictive foundation by separating variables that remain stable across domains from variables specific to each domain.

The authors develop a subspace identification theory that guarantees this separation under relaxed requirements on domain numbers and transformation properties. They use the theory to build the Subspace Identification Guarantee model through variational inference. The separation is intended to reduce the effect of domain shifts on the variables that carry invariant information.

SIG also includes class-aware conditional alignment to accommodate changes in label distributions across domains. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show better performance than existing multi-source adaptation techniques. The contribution combines a conditional theoretical guarantee for disentangling subspaces with a practical model that addresses label-distribution shifts, broadening the assumptions under which useful transfer can be pursued.
neurips-2023-subspace-identification-for.tldr: SIG separates domain-invariant and domain-specific variables under relaxed identification assumptions and accommodates changing label distributions during adaptation.

paragraphs: Recording several neuronal populations at once creates a challenge beyond describing interactions between pairs. Signals may involve different subsets of populations and evolve concurrently over time. This paper develops a dimensionality-reduction framework that summarizes this activity while retaining information about which populations participate and the direction of signal flow.

Each latent dimension describes a subset of populations, the flow among them, and how its signal evolves within and across experimental trials. The authors illustrate these capabilities in simulations and validate the method using previously studied recordings from macaque visual areas V1 and V2. This connects the framework's intended behavior to both controlled examples and neural recordings.

They then analyze simultaneous Neuropixels recordings from selected layers of V1, V2, and V3d. The method uncovers signatures of selective communication related to retinotopic alignment, the correspondence of represented visual locations across areas. These findings demonstrate how a shared framework can describe concurrent signaling patterns across more than two populations while preserving their selective structure.
neurips-2023-uncovering-motifs-of-concur.tldr: A dimensionality-reduction framework identifies participating populations, signal-flow direction, and temporal patterns in concurrent neural activity.

paragraphs: Causal representation learning seeks hidden variables whose relationships describe causal structure. This paper considers data from multiple domains that may share such a representation. The central complication is that observations are unpaired: each domain supplies its own distribution, but the data do not directly show how observations across domains belong together.

In a linear setup, the authors give sufficient conditions for identifying both the joint distribution and the shared causal graph from those separate marginal distributions. Identifiability means the available distributions uniquely determine the target structure under the stated conditions. The result therefore addresses whether reconstruction is possible before addressing how to perform it.

The authors turn the theoretical results into a practical method for recovering the shared latent causal graph. The contribution shows that missing cross-domain pairings need not prevent causal recovery when the sufficient conditions hold. Its scope remains the stated linear setting, and the existence of sufficient conditions does not imply recovery from arbitrary collections of unpaired domains.
neurips-2023-unpaired-multi-domain-causa.tldr: The paper provides sufficient conditions and a practical method for recovering shared latent causal structure from unpaired domains in a linear setting.
